done_when: A follow-up that names a period the app reads itself (a month with or without a year, a year, a quarter with or without a year, or last, previous or this month, quarter or year) answers for that period whatever window the model emits; fiscal and other wording (FY, YTD, next month, previous week) keeps the model's window and the period control; a question naming no period still inherits or aggregates as before, and an amount is never read as a year; changing an answer's period still re-runs on the chosen period

findings.body: The authoritative parser still invokes the broad `parseTimeWindow` helper before the deliberately limited named-period parser. Consequently, wording outside the Done-when list, such as “Show last 30 days”, returns `{ grain: "day", last: 30 }` and overwrites a valid model-emitted window. Non-enumerated wording is required to retain the model window, as the tests already expect for examples such as “next month” and “previous week”. Restrict the authoritative override to the enumerated month/year/quarter forms while retaining the broader parser only as a fallback when the model supplied no usable window.
findings.title: Not done: non-enumerated date wording can override the model window

findings.body: The new copula guard requires `is`, `was`, `are`, `were`, or `equals` to appear immediately before the digits. A clear amount filter such as “Show Actual is exactly 2025” therefore does not match this guard (the prefix ends in `is exactly`), reaches `calendarYear`, and replaces the model or inherited window with calendar year 2025. This still violates the requirement that an amount is never read as a year; the added matrix covers “total of exactly 2025” but not a copula followed by an amount modifier.
findings.title: Not done: amount modifiers can still be interpreted as a calendar year

findings.body: The new period matrix and edited-period test invoke `ChatService.ask` through `makeFixture`, where the model, query executor/database, audit service, dimensions, and resolver are fakes. The registered backend suite is Node-based and the frontend suite is jsdom Vitest; repository inspection still finds no Playwright test exercising the browser against a running API and real database. Thus the named-period override, inheritance/aggregation, amount protection, and period-control rerun remain proven only below the required end-to-end user-flow boundary. The successful close run executes these hermetic tests but does not supply that missing proof.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end Ask coverage for period selection and reruns

why: An Ask question that names a period, such as July 2026, answers for that period even as a follow-up in the same thread; the model's own window and the previous answer's window used to win
